source_text:
Εἰ δὲ μὴ
ἐκβάλλετέ μου τὴν μαρτυρίαν, ἐγὼ ἐμαυτῷ μαρτυρῶ. Ἡ γὰρ μαρτυρία μου ἀληθής ἐστιν, κἂν μὴ θέλητε, ἣν πρὸς Ἰουδαίους ἔλεγον· Τί με θέλετε ἀποκτεῖναι, ἄνθρωπον ὃς τὴν ἀλήθειαν ὑμῖν λελάληκα. Ἄνθρωπον εἶπεν, αἱρετικέ, μὴ οὖν θεόν. Οὗτος οὖν ὁ ἀποκτανθεὶς ἄνθρωπος Ἰησοῦς παρὰ τῶν Ἰουδαίων αὐτὸς δειλιᾷ. Καὶ μὴ συντάραττε τὸν λόγον τῇ σῇ ἀμαθείᾳ. ∆ιὰ τοῦτο δειλιῶ, ἵνα ὁ θάνατος ὡς ἀνθρώπῳ μοι συμπλακῇ καὶ ὡς παρὰ θεοῦ ἡττηθῇ. Ἀλλὰ καὶ δειλιῶν οὐ πάντη παραιτοῦμαι τὸ πάθος. Εἰ γὰρ παρῃτούμην, οὐκ ἂν εἶπον· Πάτερ εἰ δυνατὸν παρελθάτω τὸ ποτή ριον. Ἤδειν γάρ, ὅτι οὐδὲν τῷ πατρὶ ἀδύνατον. Εἰ δὲ ἐγὼ μὲν ᾔτησα παρενεχθῆναι τὸν θάνατον, αὐτὸς δὲ οὐ παρήγαγεν, δύο ἀνακύπτει ἄτοπα. Εἰ γὰρ μὴ δυνάμενος οὐ παρήνεγκεν ἢ ἀφειδῶν παρέδωκεν, εὑρίσκῃ, αἱρετικέ, ἐμοὶ μὲν δειλίαν, τῷ δὲ πατρὶ ἀδυναμίαν προσάπτων. Ἀλλ' ἐμὲ μὲν δειλιᾶν λέγων συγγνώμην ἔχεις διὰ τὴν σάρκα, τῷ δὲ πατρὶ ἀδυναμίαν προστρίβων ἀσύγγνωστα πταίεις ἀσθενεστέραν θανάτου τὴν δύναμιν λέγων τοῦ θεοῦ. Ἄλλως δὲ καὶ ἰσχυρότερόν με τοῦ πατρὸς ἀποφαίνῃ. Καὶ λέγω τὸν τρόπον. Εἰ γὰρ ἐγὼ ζῶν μὲν ἐν σαρκὶ τὸν Λάζαρον ἤγειρα, τὴν Ἰαείρου θυγατέρα, τὸν παῖδα τῆς χήρας, ἀποθανὼν δὲ πάλιν ἐν σαρκὶ ὑπὲρ τοὺς πεντακοσίους νεκροὺς ἐκ τῶν τάφων ἐσκύλευσα, ὁ δὲ πατὴρ ὁ ἐμὸς ὁ μήτε σαρκὸς μήτε θανάτου πεῖραν λαβὼν ἕνα ἐμὲ ὅνπερ ἠγάπα παῖδα, ὡς αὐτὸς λέγει· Οὗτός μού ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς ἀγαπητός, ἐξελέσθαι ἐκ κινδύνων οὐκ ἐδυνήθη, ὅρα τί πάσχεις, αἱρετικέ.
thought_title: The heretic's dilemma: if the Father did not remove the cup, either he could not or he would not
orientation: Christ continues speaking in his own defense, now turning the heretic's charge back on him: if the Father did not remove the cup, the heretic must accuse either the Son of fear or the Father of powerlessness.
pass_a_gloss: But if not, you reject my testimony; I bear witness to myself. For my testimony is true, even if you do not wish it, which I was saying to the Jews: Why do you wish to kill me, a man who has spoken the truth to you? He said 'man,' heretic, not therefore God. This man Jesus, then, who was killed by the Jews, he himself fears. And do not confuse the Word with your ignorance. For this reason I fear, so that death may grapple with me as with a man and may be defeated as by God. But even fearing, I do not entirely refuse the passion. For if I refused, I would not have said: Father, if it is possible, let the cup pass. For I knew that nothing is impossible for the Father. But if I asked that death be carried away, and he did not bring it about, two absurdities arise. For if he did not carry it away because he was not able, or he handed me over because he was without mercy, you are found, heretic, attaching fear to me and powerlessness to the Father. But saying that I fear, you have excuse because of the flesh, but by attributing powerlessness to the Father you sin unforgivably, saying that the power of God is weaker than death. And otherwise you also show me to be stronger than the Father. And I will tell the manner. For if I, living in the flesh, raised Lazarus, the daughter of Jairus, the son of the widow, and dying again in the flesh I plundered more than five hundred dead from the tombs, but my Father, who had no experience of flesh or death, was not able to rescue one child, me, whom he loved, as he himself says: This is my beloved son, from dangers, see what you suffer, heretic.

choices.why: ἀφειδῶν means 'not sparing' or 'without mercy,' indicating the Father would have handed him over out of lack of care, not persistence.
The phrase means the heretic is excused or has allowance for saying the Son fears, because of the flesh; it is not Christ granting pardon.
The noun is plural, referring to the multiple dangers of death and passion from which the Father could not rescue.
ἄτοπα means 'out of place' or 'absurd' conclusions, fitting the rhetorical dilemma Christ poses.
σκυλεύω means to strip or plunder spoils, fitting the image of Christ despoiling the tombs of the dead.

pass_b_english: But if you do not throw out my testimony, I testify about myself. For my testimony is true, even if you do not want it to be—the testimony I spoke to the Jews: “Why do you want to kill me, a man who has spoken the truth to you?” (John 8:40). He said “a man,” heretic—not God. So this man Jesus, killed by the Jews, is the one who fears. And do not confuse the Word with your ignorance. I fear for this reason: so that death may grapple with me as with a man, and be defeated as by God. But even in fearing, I do not entirely refuse the passion. For if I refused it, I would not have said, “Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass” (Matthew 26:39). For I knew that nothing is impossible for the Father. But if I asked for death to be carried away, and he did not carry it away, two absurdities arise. For if he did not carry it away because he was unable, or because he spared not and handed me over, then you are found, heretic, attaching fear to me and powerlessness to the Father. But when you say that I fear, you are pardoned because of the flesh; yet when you attribute powerlessness to the Father, you sin without excuse, saying that the power of God is weaker than death. And in another way you make me out to be stronger than the Father. Let me tell you how. For if I, while living in the flesh, raised Lazarus, Jairus’s daughter, and the widow’s son, and after dying in the flesh, again plundered more than five hundred dead from their tombs, but my Father—who had no experience of flesh or death—could not rescue me, his beloved Son, from dangers—as he himself says, “This is my beloved Son” (Matthew 3:17)—then see what you are getting into, heretic.

problems.quote: could not rescue me, his one beloved child, as he himself says, "This is my beloved Son" (Matthew 3:17), from dangers
problems.source_quote: ἐξελέσθαι ἐκ κινδύνων οὐκ ἐδυνήθη, ὅρα τί πάσχεις, αἱρετικέ
problems.why: Word order distorts syntax: 'from dangers' belongs with 'could not rescue', but the parenthetical quotation splits it awkwardly; 'one beloved child' adds 'one' not in source (ἕνα is 'one' but goes with 'me whom he loved').
problems.fix: could not rescue me, his beloved Son, from dangers—as he himself says, "This is my beloved Son"—see what you suffer, heretic.

edits.old: could not rescue me, his one beloved child, as he himself says, “This is my beloved Son” (Matthew 3:17), from dangers, then see what you are doing, heretic.
edits.new: could not rescue me, his beloved Son, from dangers—as he himself says, “This is my beloved Son” (Matthew 3:17)—then see what you are doing, heretic.

fixed: Fixed word order: 'from dangers' now directly follows 'could not rescue me', and the parenthetical quotation no longer splits the syntax. Removed 'one' (ἕνα modifies 'me whom he loved', not 'child').

problems.quote: or handed me over without mercy
problems.why: ἀφειδῶν means 'sparing not' / 'without regard for,' not 'without mercy.' The Father's lack of concern for Christ's suffering, not mercy, is at issue.
problems.fix: or because he spared me not handed me over

problems.quote: you have excuse because of the flesh
problems.why: συγγνώμην ἔχεις means 'you are pardoned/forgiven,' not 'you have excuse.' The heretic is granted pardon for attributing fear to Christ due to the flesh.
problems.fix: you are pardoned because of the flesh

problems.quote: after dying again in the flesh
problems.why: πάλιν modifies 'plundered,' not 'dying again.' Christ died once; he plundered the dead 'again' (as he had raised them while living).
problems.fix: and after dying in the flesh, again plundered
problems.ruling: πάλιν modifies ἐσκύλευσα (plundered again), not ἀποθανών; Christ died once, plundered again as when living.

problems.quote: then see what you are doing
problems.why: πάσχεις means 'you suffer' / 'what you suffer,' not 'what you are doing.' The heretic suffers harm/damage from his own argument.
problems.fix: then see what you suffer, heretic
problems.ruling: πάσχεις means 'you suffer,' not 'you are doing'; ὅρα τί πάσχεις = 'see what you suffer,' a real meaning change.

πάλιν modifies 'plundered,' not 'dying'; changed to 'after dying in the flesh, again plundered.'
πάσχεις means 'you suffer,' not 'you are doing'; changed to 'then see what you suffer, heretic.'

problems.quote: or because he spared me not handed me over
problems.why: Greek says 'or sparing not he handed over'; English omits 'handed over' and garbles the sense.
problems.fix: or because he spared not and handed me over

problems.quote: then see what you suffer, heretic
problems.why: πάσχεις means 'you experience/undergo,' not 'suffer' in sense of pain; 'see what you are undergoing'—the absurd position you're in.
problems.fix: see what you are getting into, heretic

fixed: mistranslation: 'or because he spared me not handed me over' garbles the source 'ἢ ἀφειδῶν παρέδωκεν' ('or sparing not he handed over'); fixed to 'or because he spared not and handed me over'.
mistranslation: 'then see what you suffer, heretic' misreads 'ὅρα τί πάσχεις' as suffering pain; fixed to 'then see what you are getting into, heretic' to convey the absurd position.

dismissed.quote: because he spared not and handed me over
dismissed.why: ἀφειδῶν means 'sparing [me]' or 'showing no mercy,' not 'sparing not.' The sense is 'because he spared me not' or 'because he was merciless.'
dismissed.note: ἀφειδῶν means 'unsparing', so 'spared not' gives the right sense and echoes Romans 8:32; the checker misreads the word.
